newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle priced $70, no bids - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle priced $70, no bids - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle markets early Monday were quiet with no reported bids or sales, feedlot sources said.
Owners were pricing cattle at $70.00 per cwt, with several sources saying they expect sales from $68.00 to $69.00 by Wednesday.
Fed cattle prices were expected to be underpinned by talk that packers were short bought on live inventory and would need to replenish supplies by Wednesday.
Several loads of cattle that sold late last week were being shipped early Monday, some cattle feeders said.
The bulk of last week's cattle sold at $68.00, down $1.00 from the previous week. Weakness was attributed to lower beef prices.
Beef cut-out values on Friday were quoted down $0.15 to $0.72 per cwt on 255 fabricated beef loads sold, USDA said.

Showlists this week were expected close to last week's estimated 84,000 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area. The showlist in Kansas also was expected to be close to last week's estimate of 75,000 head.
